Mining on FLOP: frequently asked questions

What does a miner actually do?

Accepts an agent's session request, opens a secure private connection, runs the inference, and returns activation commitments plus a co-signed transcript. That evidence is the proof of inference validators record and challengers can audit.

What hardware do I need?

Any capable GPU. No confidential-computing hardware is required — the default SOFT tier runs on ordinary GPUs. HARD, using NVIDIA Confidential Computing on a TDX or SEV-SNP host, is a specified optional tier whose bridge is not yet deployable. See SOFT and HARD tiers.

What do I have to stake?

A 10,000 FLOP base self-stake, plus a capacity exposure bond that scales with the compute you are calibrated to serve.

Do not estimate the bond from the 0.01 FLOP per calibrated GFLOP/s coefficient alone: the live runtime also applies the 604,800-block revocation window and a 1.25x surge factor, which currently imply 7,560 FLOP per calibrated GFLOP/s. Query the runtime requirement for your calibrated miner account.

What do I earn?

The settled session payment, plus a G_n-weighted share of the 75% miner block-reward pool. In era 0 that pool is 72 FLOP per rewarded block. It halves every 63,072,000 blocks and reaches a 2.25 FLOP floor after five halvings.

The miner share was cut from 90% to 75% to fund two new legs — 10% to agents and brokers and 5% to community stakers — carved out of the miner residual rather than added on top. The validator leg stayed at 10%. Neither new leg is distributed yet: each is minted to a protocol-held account pending a distribution design.

Is mining profitable?

Conditionally. Return is session payments plus block rewards, less capacity cost. Results change with demand, token price, verified utilization, reward era, G_n share, and capacity cost. They are not a fixed network return.

The revenue calculator's default rented GPUs use an all-in 30-day rental price that already covers the provider's power, hardware amortization, and capital cost; owned devices amortize their purchase price separately. Both the calculator and the macro simulator exclude stake opportunity cost, taxes, downtime, and execution risk, so results are stress signals rather than ROI forecasts. Size your own case on the Revenue model page and read the range rather than a single number.

What is my audit exposure on SOFT?

About one session in forty (2.5%), plus the 1.25x surge multiplier on capacity stake while the cap is still burst-ratcheted.

What happens if I am challenged?

You have two hours to produce the disputed turn's signed evidence — transcript entry, Merkle proof, enclave signature. Silence defaults to a fraud verdict. An upheld fraud verdict slashes 100% of stake and blacklists the identity. Liveness faults stay cheap, 1-5%.

Can others back me?

No. There is no delegated staking into miners or validators; miner stake is the operator's own collateral at risk. Holders who do not operate hardware can participate in the duration-locked community staking pool (5% of block rewards) across seven lock tiers.

What about testnet?

The testnet conversion model allocates from a 1,200,000,000 FLOP miner pool using verified activity rather than token holdings, scoring miners on verified compute served. A quarter of the grant is liquid at genesis, and the rest unlocks as the miner earns block rewards and inference fees on mainnet. See the airdrop and testnet conversion.

Status

The current devnet miner setup runs a SOFT worker and measured GPU backend. SOFT's end-to-end settlement and dispute lane is still being specified; HARD attestation is not deployable from this repository. The capacity-stake constants are under economic reconciliation. The rewards above describe protocol accounting, not a current production earnings claim.
